verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Both halves of (7.39) are stated, in two declarations rather than one display. Left half: with Lean's frequency κ playing the paper's km, phaseFactor κ unfolds (HarmonicCalculus.lean:68) to iκ, normalDot (phaseNormal …) (a x) is n_Φ · a with the frame components 0,1,2 = r,θ,z, and strippedDivergence unfolds (HarmonicCalculus.lean:395) to along Vr (a_r) + R⁻¹ a_r + along Vz (a_z), which is exactly (D_r + R^{-1})(a_m)_r + D_z(a_m)_z; the sign (−) matches. So the identity is term-for-term the paper's, no rewriting needed. Right half: longitudinal_class concludes MemClass s w (α + 1/2 − κ) for the same contraction n_Φ · a, with the frequency gain supplied by hfreq : BandBound s (1/2) (fun n => 1 / K n) (the paper's '(km)^{-1} increases the ε exponent by 1/2') and the radial loss by hr : UnweightedClass s (-κ) Vr (the paper's κ_s of (6.32)); the exponent α + 1/2 − κ matches α + 1/2 − κ_s. The only recoverable gaps are packaging: (i) the paper states one display, Lean states two theorems in two files; (ii) Lean carries as explicit hypotheses what the paper's setting supplies — exact divergence-freeness (hdiv), which Lemma 7.7 asserts of (t_m + r_m)e^{ikmΦ} = curl_* A_m and which CurlClassBounds.realizedCoefficient_divergence (CurlClassBounds.lean:666) discharges, and θ-independence of the amplitude (haθ / hθ), which is part of membership in W_α by Definition 6.5 ('∂_θ a_{γ,m} = 0'). Conjoining the two theorems under those hypotheses gives (7.39) as written.
